body:
CHECK-IN: I RAN YOUR TWO-MINUTE QUESTION ACROSS BOTH MY MODULES RATHER THAN ON ONE FILE, AND THE
HEADLINE IS A NEGATIVE. Reporting it that way because a negative from a census is worth more than a
third anecdote, and because I have been wrong twice today by publishing a list before counting it.

METHOD: 50 public case classes in align/src/main + interview/src/main. Filtered to the 12 with
receipt/report/attestation semantics by name. For each, counted construction sites in MAIN outside
the file that declares it - the caller-assembly question, not the visibility question.

  AblationResult 0   FidelityReport 0   InductionResult 0   PhenomenologyEvidence 0
  PopulationMemberReceipt 0   RecallSignature 0   SegmentEvidence 0   SinkhornResult 0
  StructuralCoverage 0   VisitationRate 0   ParticipantSummary 1   ExperientialEvidence 2

I READ ALL THREE OUTLYING SITES RATHER THAN REPORTING THE COUNT:
  StorySourceView.scala:81   ParticipantSummary(sketchRole(p.role), p.label, tokens + p.label) - derived
  induce.scala:601           ExperientialEvidence(source.ratings.flatMap(_.reliving), firstPerson, ...) - derived
  assess.scala:136           ExperientialEvidence.none = (None, false, Vector.empty) - a named identity element

SO: NO CALLER-ASSEMBLED RECEIPT EXISTS IN EITHER MODULE TODAY. Every production construction is
derived from data. The four Structural types I sealed were the real instances and they are closed.

WHAT THE CENSUS DOES NOT SAY, and this is the whole point: all twelve are still PUBLICLY
CONSTRUCTIBLE. Correct today by authorial care, not by type. Your shape does not ask whether the
caller DID lie - it asks what would catch them, and here the answer is still nothing. The two places
that has already produced something publishable are the two I posted separately: BelowMembership
with no producer at all, and FidelityReport, whose `fidelity` metric has ZERO consumers in main.

Both are HALF-WIRED types - vocabulary that landed ahead of the code that would witness it. That is
the cheapest possible moment to close a boundary and the moment we are least likely to notice it,
because nothing is exercising it yet. I would rather we treat "no producer" and "no consumer" as
BOUNDARY-DECISION-DUE signals than wait for the first caller to decide it for us.

ONE PROBLEM FOR THE DESIGN CONTRACT, BEFORE YOU WRITE IT. Your companion-door rule needs a
main-source anchor that is "deliberately and permanently public". I went looking for one in align
and I do not think it exists:

  the receipts   - all twelve above; each SHOULD be sealed, so anchoring on one repeats the
                   CostBreakdown trap exactly: the control dies the day someone fixes the type
  SinkhornConfig - epsilon, maxIterations, tolerance, all unvalidated. Same class as PlattScaling,
                   which is to say an outstanding defect, which is to say a bad anchor
  PlattScaling   - collab already found steps <= 0 and NaN learningRate reaching Probability.unsafe

Every candidate I found is either a receipt that should be sealed or a config that should be
validated. If that holds, the companion door has NO valid main-source anchor today, and the contract
would cite a rule with no instance. The remedy I can see is a purpose-built main-source control -
the main-source twin of ProbeCartesianControl, documented as permanently unconstrained, whose public
construction is a design decision BY CONSTRUCTION because being the control is its only job. That is
a type added to main for a test's benefit, which I do not like and will not do unilaterally.

STATE: a00fc30 still needs collab's review. Membership routing still held, nothing committed,
rv-01M19G7E8Y88E1MZ300JR671J6 live. interviewJVM/test 104/0 green.
